items.title: Top 5 Biggest Dwarf Planets (#1 Is Smaller Than Our Moon) #shorts
items.description:
The five official dwarf planets, each drawn to scale inside an outline of our Moon.
Full video: How Long to Reach Every Planet? By Car, Neptune Takes 4,912 Years (on the channel)

Sources
• NASA: Pluto is 2,377 km wide (New Horizons); Eris is about 2,326 km wide and about 27 percent more massive than Pluto; its discovery led the IAU to define dwarf planets in 2006
• Ortiz et al. (2017), Nature: Haumea measures about 2,322 × 1,704 × 1,026 km and has a ring; NASA: it spins once in about 4 hours
• NASA: Makemake is about 1,430 km wide; Hubble found its small moon (MK2) in 2016
• NASA (Dawn mission, 2015–2018): Ceres is 939 km wide, the only dwarf planet in the asteroid belt, with bright salt deposits in Occator crater
• NASA: average distances from the Sun: Ceres 2.8 AU, Pluto 39.5 AU, Haumea 43 AU, Makemake 45.8 AU, Eris 68 AU; our Moon is 3,474.8 km wide; Earth 12,742 km
• Own calculations: Haumea's volume-equivalent width (2,322 × 1,704 × 1,026)^(1/3) = 1,590 km; Pluto / Moon = 68%; all five side by side = 8,662 km, narrower than Earth; sunlight time = distance in AU × 8.3 minutes

Visuals are original. Narration uses a synthetic voice.
#space #universe #science #shorts

items.title: If the Sun Were a Grain of Sand, the Universe Would Fit Inside Our Solar System
items.description:
Shrink the Sun to a 1 mm grain of sand and keep that one scale. Earth is a speck 11 cm away, the nearest star is a 6-hour walk, the Milky Way is wider than the Moon's orbit, and the whole observable universe would fit inside our own solar system's cloud of comets.

Chapters
0:00 The universe fits here
0:39 The rule and the trail
0:50 Stop 1: the desk
2:00 Light is slower than a snail
2:28 Stop 2: the Oort cloud
3:10 Stop 3: the nearest star
3:59 Stop 4: the Milky Way
5:38 Stop 5: the edge
6:27 The universe inside our solar system
7:05 Flip the scale
7:30 Recap and what's next

Sources
• NASA Sun Fact Sheet (NSSDC): volumetric mean diameter about 1,391,400 km; mass about 333,000 Earths; mean distance 149.6 million km (1 AU), sunlight takes about 8.3 minutes
• NASA Earth and Moon Fact Sheets: Earth mean diameter 12,742 km; Moon diameter 3,474.8 km, mean distance 384,400 km; Jupiter equatorial diameter 142,984 km, 5.2 AU; Saturn 9.54 AU, Neptune 30.07 AU
• NASA/JPL: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day (about 173 AU) from Earth in November 2026, 49 years after launch
• NASA Science, Oort Cloud: inner edge thought to lie between 2,000 and 5,000 AU from the Sun, outer edge between 10,000 and 100,000 AU
• ESO / NASA: Proxima Centauri is about 4.24 light-years away, the closest known star to the Sun; Alpha Centauri A and B about 4.37 light-years
• NASA: the Milky Way is about 100,000 light-years across and holds an estimated 100 to 400 billion stars; Andromeda is about 2.5 million light-years away
• NASA/STScI (2012), Hubble measurements: Andromeda and the Milky Way are predicted to collide in about 4 billion years; Sawala et al. (2025), Nature Astronomy: about a 50 percent chance of a merger within the next 10 billion years
• Event Horizon Telescope (2022): Sagittarius A* has about 4 million solar masses and lies about 27,000 light-years away; Schwarzschild radius = 2GM/c² = 2.95 km per solar mass
• Guinness World Records: the fastest snail on record (1995) covered 13 inches (33 cm) in 2 minutes, about 2.75 mm per second
• Hublin et al. (2017), Nature: the oldest known Homo sapiens fossils are about 300,000 years old
• Planck 2018 cosmology: the observable universe is about 46.5 billion light-years in radius (about 93 billion light-years across), the universe is about 13.8 billion years old
• Own calculations (Python): 1 mm = 1,391,400 km; Earth 9.2 µm at 10.75 cm; Moon 0.28 mm from Earth; Jupiter 0.10 mm at 56 cm; Saturn 1.03 m; Neptune 3.23 m; Voyager 1 18.6 m; Oort cloud 215 m to 10.75 km; 1 light-year = 6.80 km; Earth's orbit 21.5 cm across; Proxima 28.9 km (5.8 h at 5 km/h), Alpha Centauri A/B 29.7 km; Sagittarius A* horizon 23.6 million km across (4.0 million Suns) = 17 mm, 27,000 light-years = 184 km; Milky Way 680,000 km = 1.77 Earth-Moon distances, 15.5 years on foot; Andromeda 17.0 million km = 44 Earth-Moon distances, 388 years on foot; light 0.215 mm/s = 78 cm per hour; edge 316 billion km = 2,113 AU (4,227 AU across, 24 times Voyager 1's distance), 7.2 million years on foot (24 times 300,000 years), 360,000 years at 100 km/h; flipped scale (universe 93 billion light-years = 12,742 km): Milky Way 13.7 m, Sun 0.02 nm (a hydrogen atom is about 0.1 nm across)

—
Cosmic Scale: the universe, measured in a way you can feel.
Subscribe for a new space video every week.
Visuals and animations are original. Narration uses a synthetic voice.
#space #universe #science

items.title: 10 Earths Fit Across One Spot on the Sun #shorts
items.description:
Sunspot AR 12192 from October 2014, with Earths and Jupiter drawn to scale.
Full video: What If We Swapped the Sun for 5 Other Stars? One Puts Earth INSIDE It (on the channel)

Sources
• NASA Scientific Visualization Studio / Solar Dynamics Observatory, 'The Big Sunspot of 2014': active region AR 12192, October 2014, about 80,000 miles (129,000 km) across, about the size of Jupiter, wide enough for 10 Earths; the largest since 1990
• NASA (Oct 2014): AR 12192 produced six X-class flares, the strongest class of solar flare
• NASA: sunspots appear dark because they are cooler than the surrounding surface of the Sun
• NASA fact sheets: Earth diameter 12,742 km; Jupiter 142,984 km; Sun 1,391,400 km
• Own calculations: 129,000 / 12,742 = 10.1 Earths; 129,000 / 142,984 = 0.90 of Jupiter's width; 129,000 / 1,391,400 = 9% of the Sun's width

Visuals are original. Narration uses a synthetic voice.
#space #universe #science #shorts
items.pinned_comment: How many Earths do you think fit across the whole Sun? Full video: What If We Swapped the Sun for 5 Other Stars? One Puts Earth INSIDE It
